title: Mighty Mouse
shortOutcome: A provider-agnostic reliability harness that gives AI coding agents structured protocols and project-native verification.
role: Creator, systems engineer, and evaluation designer
ownership: Original reliability harness, versioned protocols, project verifier, evaluation design, packaging, CLI, MCP transport, platform rules, CI, and study execution. Foundation models, model runtimes, MCP itself, and agent platforms are third-party systems.

basis.generalizationBoundary: Ten paired tasks from the recorded projects, agent, models, and environment only; no generalized reliability or speed improvement was demonstrated.

evidence.label: First-attempt passes
evidence.detail: Mighty Mouse and the control each passed six of ten paired real-project tasks on the first attempt, with zero scope violations in both conditions.
evidence.limitation: The study did not demonstrate better generalized first-pass reliability.

basis.generalizationBoundary: Ten paired tasks from the recorded projects, agent, models, and environment only; no generalized reliability or speed improvement was demonstrated.

evidence.label: Retry rounds
evidence.detail: Mighty Mouse used four retry rounds across the sample; the control used six.
evidence.limitation: Two fewer retries in this sample is not evidence of a universal improvement.

basis.generalizationBoundary: Ten paired tasks from the recorded projects, agent, models, and environment only; no generalized reliability or speed improvement was demonstrated.

evidence.label: Mean blind-review quality
evidence.detail: Mighty Mouse received a 4.60 mean blind-review score versus 4.30 for the control across the ten paired tasks.
evidence.limitation: The quality difference belongs to this sample and its recorded blind-review procedure.

basis.generalizationBoundary: Ten paired tasks from the recorded projects, agent, models, and environment only; no generalized reliability or speed improvement was demonstrated.

evidence.label: Median duration
evidence.detail: Mighty Mouse was slower: 262.5 seconds median duration versus 229.5 seconds for the control; raw mean duration was also slower.
evidence.limitation: The study did not demonstrate a generalized speed improvement.

basis.generalizationBoundary: Historical synthetic promotion suite and recorded environment only; the later prospective real-project study did not reproduce a generalized speed or first-pass reliability improvement.

evidence.label: Historical synthetic latency result
evidence.detail: Lean reduced average latency by 29.5% while both conditions passed 15 of 15 tasks in the historical synthetic promotion suite.
evidence.limitation: This historical synthetic result is bounded to that suite and must not be generalized to real project work.

problem.title: Agent output is not proof that a coding task is complete.
body: Coding agents can produce plausible explanations and still miss required files, violate scope, or stop before the project’s own checks pass. The operational problem is turning a model response into a bounded, inspectable result another person can trust.

Mighty Mouse supplies versioned complexity protocols, project-native verification, structured results, and a bounded retry contract. The model and agent platform remain replaceable; the reliability layer stays explicit.

ownership.title: I built the reliability layer, not the models or agent platforms.
body: I designed and built the harness, versioned protocols, project verifier, result schema, CLI, MCP transport, packaging, platform rules, CI, evaluation fixtures, and prospective study.
Foundation models, model runtimes, MCP itself, and platforms such as Codex and Antigravity are third-party systems. Mighty Mouse integrates with them; it does not claim their underlying work.

systemMap.label: Task + complexity input
systemMap.detail: A coding task enters with an explicit complexity level or a deterministic default.

systemMap.label: Protocol selection
systemMap.detail: The harness returns a versioned low, medium, or high-complexity execution contract.

systemMap.label: Agent execution
systemMap.detail: The chosen agent works inside declared scope using the project’s existing tools and conventions.

systemMap.label: Project-native verification
systemMap.detail: Tests, lint, build, scope, and changed-file checks run as structured verification steps.

systemMap.label: Bounded retry loop
systemMap.detail: Failures return specific next steps; the agent may retry without entering an unbounded correction cycle.

systemMap.label: Structured result
systemMap.detail: Pass state, checks, warnings, and suggestions are returned in a stable human- and machine-readable form.

systemMap.label: Stop condition
systemMap.detail: A passing result completes the task; exhausted retries or unresolved scope failures stop and escalate.

decisions.title: Use the project’s checks as the authority
decisions.decision: Return executable test, lint, build, and scope results instead of treating the agent’s explanation as completion evidence.
decisions.consequence: A persuasive response cannot hide a failing project state.

decisions.title: Keep retries bounded
decisions.decision: Pair structured failure suggestions with an explicit retry ceiling rather than allowing open-ended self-correction.
decisions.consequence: The workflow has a visible escalation point and a measurable retry cost.

decisions.title: Publish the mixed result
decisions.decision: Retain the tied first-pass rate and slower durations beside the favorable retry and blind-review results.
decisions.consequence: The case study demonstrates evaluation discipline without claiming a generalized improvement the study did not show.

buildRecord.label: 01 / INTERFACE
buildRecord.title: Core CLI
buildRecord.detail: Protocol and verify commands expose stable JSON interfaces alongside doctor, demo, and benchmark operations.

buildRecord.label: 02 / TRANSPORT
buildRecord.title: MCP server
buildRecord.detail: A separate package exposes protocol and verification tools over stdio for compatible agent platforms.

buildRecord.label: 03 / DISTRIBUTE
buildRecord.title: Installable packages
buildRecord.detail: Core and MCP wheels and source distributions are built, archive-inspected, checksummed, and smoke-tested outside the checkout.

buildRecord.label: 04 / VERIFY
buildRecord.title: CI and paired evaluation
buildRecord.detail: Python 3.10–3.13 CI, packaging gates, frozen trial manifests, and blind reviews keep implementation and claims auditable.

failures.title: The synthetic suite hit a ceiling
failures.observed: Mighty Mouse, the historical protocol conditions, and a bare control all passed the frozen synthetic tasks, limiting what the suite could prove about reliability.
failures.response: Bound the 29.5% latency result to its recorded environment and ran a prospective paired study on real project tasks.

failures.title: The real-project result was mixed
failures.observed: First-attempt passes tied at 6/10, and Mighty Mouse was slower by both mean and median duration despite fewer retries and higher mean blind-review quality.
failures.response: Published the unfavorable timing and tied reliability results and stated that no generalized improvement was demonstrated.

failures.title: macOS metadata contaminated package inputs
failures.observed: AppleDouble resource-fork files created noisy Git and archive failures on the external volume.
failures.response: Added package-data exclusions, source-distribution filtering, archive inspection, and explicit regression tests.

failures.title: Editable installs and Python 3.10 exposed packaging gaps
failures.observed: Custom build-backend behavior and older-Python compatibility failed outside the original development environment.
failures.response: Completed editable-build hooks, added compatibility dependencies, and required clean Python 3.10–3.13 CI plus artifact-only installation smokes.

currentStatus.title: Released reliability tooling with bounded evidence.
body: Version 0.2.1 ships the core library, CLI, MCP transport, platform rules, verifier, CI matrix, release artifacts, and the completed ten-pair study. The current evidence supports fewer retries and higher mean blind-review quality in this sample, not a generalized first-pass reliability or speed improvement.
